title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, sautéed, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs are dark meat cuts rich in protein and healthy fats. When sautéed in a little oil the skin becomes crispy while the meat stays juicy. These cuts are common in Asian, Mediterranean and comfort‑food dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark meat contains more iron and zinc than white meat.
Chicken legs and thighs are often grilled or cooked “tandoori” where the skin helps retain moisture.
Proper sautéing creates a flavorful crust rich in aromatic compounds.
In many cultures dark meat is considered more “satisfying” than breast meat.
Chicken thighs can be used to make bone broth that is high in collagen.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains beneficial fats
items.content: The skin supplies monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Provides iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Phosphorus and a modest amount of calcium in the meat contribute to strong bones.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The crispy skin adds calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C to prevent salmonella and campylobacter.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to chicken proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté, bake, grill or braise the pieces. Season with salt, pepper, paprika, garlic or rosemary before cooking. Serve with vegetables, rice, potatoes or in salads and wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw cuts in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked meat can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of ≥ 75 °C before eating.
